newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries to buy Taormina.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries to buy Taormina.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc. said Wednesday it will acquire Taormina Industries Inc., one of the largest privately held waste companies in California, for about $250 million in stock.
Taormina, based in Anaheim, Calif., hauls solid waste for more than one million customers in Southern California.

"The addition of Taormina Industries is consistent with our strategy to expand rapidly in growing markets across the United States," said Harris Hudson, vice chairman of Republic and chairman of its solid waste division.
"This acquisition gives our waste division a significant presence in Southern California and establishes a solid foundation for future growth."
Republic, based in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., said it expects to close the deal, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, by the end of February.
Republic, led by Florida billionaire Wayne Huizenga, has also been acquiring a string of auto dealerships in a bid to build up a nationwide network.
On Tuesday, Republic announced a definitive agreement to acquire Courtesy Auto Group Inc., which owns and operates a variety of car dealerships in the Orlando area, for about $30 million in stock.
Republic's stock rose 25 cents to $39.75 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
